description: Integration tests for the CLI layer, validating subprocess execution, argument forwarding, dry-run output, edge cases, and setup-to-execute composition

userStories.title: Unit tests for findFeatureDirs
userStories.description: As a developer, I want direct tests for findFeatureDirs so that feature directory discovery is validated independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: returns empty array when .scratch/ does not exist
Test: returns empty array when .scratch/ has directories without issues/ subdirs
Test: returns entries with correct name, dir, and spec paths for valid feature dirs
Each test creates and cleans up its own temp directory
userStories.notes: findFeatureDirs is already exported from src/index.ts -- import it directly

userStories.title: Unit tests for resolveIssuesDir with explicit flags
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify that when both --dir and --spec are provided, resolveIssuesDir returns them directly without scanning .scratch/.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: returns { dir, spec } exactly as given when both flags are provided
No filesystem scanning occurs (the temp dir has no .scratch/)
userStories.notes: resolveIssuesDir is already exported from src/index.ts

userStories.title: Subprocess CLI smoke test for execute
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a test that spawns node dist/index.js <provider> as a child process so that I know the yargs wiring, argument parsing, and file resolution work end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: Test spawns the built CLI with --dir, --spec, and --timeout-secs pointing at a temp directory with ticket files
Uses the existing mock-agent-pass.js as the provider argument
Asserts ticket files on disk are updated to **Status:** done
Asserts log files are created in the expected location

userStories.title: Create mock-agent-echo-args and test --model flag
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify that --model (or -m) is passed through to the spawned agent process so that running npx nightralph claude -m claude-sonnet-4-6 actually forwards the model argument.
acceptanceCriteria: Create test/mock-agent-echo-args.js that writes process.argv to stdout, then exits 0
Test spawns the CLI with -m test-model using this mock agent
Asserts the log file contains --model and test-model in the captured argv

userStories.title: Subprocess CLI test for --dry-run
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a test that runs the CLI with --dry-run so that I know the dry-run path works through yargs and produces the expected output.
acceptanceCriteria: Test spawns the built CLI with --dry-run, --dir, and --spec
Asserts output contains Wave 1: with the expected ticket filenames
Asserts output contains AGENT INSTRUCTIONS (prompt preview)
Asserts ticket files on disk are NOT modified

userStories.title: CLI exits gracefully when no tickets found
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify the CLI handles the empty-directory edge case gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: Test points --dir at an empty directory with a valid --spec
Asserts stdout contains No ticket files found
Asserts exit code 0 (graceful, not a crash)

userStories.title: CLI exits with error for missing dir/spec
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the CLI to fail clearly when --dir or --spec point to nonexistent paths.

userStories.title: Unknown blocker warning and stripping
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify that runExecute warns about blockers referencing nonexistent ticket numbers and strips them so execution proceeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Test creates a ticket with **Blocked by:** 99 where ticket 99 does not exist
Spawns the CLI as a subprocess
Asserts stderr/stdout contains a warning mentioning blocker 99
Asserts the ticket still completes (blocker was stripped)

userStories.title: Dry-run deadlock detection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the dry-run to report deadlocked tickets (circular dependencies) so users can fix their ticket graph before running real agents.
acceptanceCriteria: Test creates two tickets that block each other (1 blocks 2, 2 blocks 1)
Asserts output contains Deadlocked tickets with both filenames

userStories.title: Setup-then-execute composition test
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a test that runs setup, then creates issue files in the expected .scratch/ layout, then runs execute -- proving the two commands compose correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Test calls setup() with tracker:'local' in a temp project dir
Creates .scratch/<feature>/issues/ with 2 ticket files and a spec.md
Spawns the CLI as a subprocess pointing at that project dir (using the mock agent)
userStories.notes: Most complex test -- calls setup() as a library function, then spawns CLI for execute
